title: Coordinate integrals imply the diagonal-kernel triangles
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring and f:X->Y a proper morphism of schemes. Work on ordinary unbounded small-etale A-module derived categories. Put W=X times_Y X with projections p1,p2 and diagonal Delta. Let B be a complex on X and let d be a trace-diagonal datum: t:Rf! B->A_Y and delta:RDelta! A_X->p2*B. Let J be a lisse rank-one A-module sheaf on Y, n an integer, L=J[2n], and e:B~f*L. Use canonical compact-support exchange and composition, and the normalized signed tensor comparisons [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons, lem-kun-tensor-sym, lem-kun-tensor-unit]. Define t1=beta1^(-1) followed by f*t and the pullback unit, and t2=Rp2!(coordinate_e^(-1)) followed by beta2^(-1), f*t and the pullback unit; coordinate_e:p1*B~p2*B is induced by e and equality of the two maps to Y. Let alpha_i:A_X~Rp_i! RDelta! A_X be the canonical identity/composition comparisons for p_i Delta=id. Suppose alpha_i followed by Rp_i!(delta) and t_i is identity for i=1,2. Form the natural unit by tensoring the supported diagonal with p1*M, pushing along p2, applying inverse projection and inverse proper exchange, and transporting to H(K)=B tensor f*K by the canonical symmetry. Form epsilon by inverse PF_{B,K}, t tensor identity and the left unitor. Then for all M and K, Rf!(eta_M) followed by epsilon_{Rf!M} is identity and eta_{HK} followed by H(epsilon_K) is identity.

source.place: Both coordinate diagonal integrals and their two triangle computations, followed by the inverse-projection trace counit.

proof.text: Factor the specified unit component as I_delta(M) followed by C_B(M). This is the associativity identity proved in unit_app_eq. The specified counit component is epsilon_t by definition. Apply the diagonal-free compact-support coordinate contractions.

For the first triangle, expand F of the unit factorization and use the first contraction. Functoriality reassociates it as F(I_delta);D;F(pi_p1 inverse), followed by F(identity tensor t1 then rho). Use the first insertion-projection equation. Combine tensor maps into tensor with alpha1(1);P1(delta);t1. The first integral hypothesis sets this to identity; cancel the right unitor and its inverse inside F, then use F.map_id.

For the second triangle apply the second contraction at K after the unit factorization, and reassociate. The second insertion-projection equation leaves rho inverse followed by tensor with alpha2(1);P2(delta);t2, then rho. The second integral hypothesis, tensor functoriality, and inverse-unitor cancellation give identity. No geometric hypothesis is added.

theorem triangles (J : Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))
    (hJ : Scheme.IsLisseRankOneSheaf J) (n : ℤ)
    (e : B ≅ (CoordinateTrace.pull A f).obj (CoordinateTrace.shiftedLine A J n))
    (h : Integrals A d (CoordinateTrace.shiftedLine A J n) e) :
    (∀ M : DerivedCategoryModule A X,
      (rightDerivedLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).map ((unit A d).app M) ≫
        (counit A d).app
          ((rightDerivedLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).obj M) = 𝟙 _) ∧
    (∀ K : DerivedCategoryModule A Y,
      (unit A d).app
          ((CoordinateTrace.pull A f ⋙
            (derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).obj B).obj K) ≫
        (CoordinateTrace.pull A f ⋙ (derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).obj B).map
          ((counit A d).app K) = 𝟙 _)
